record.file_problem: This is repository metadata, README, and file list only; source code and notebooks were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README describes extracting a refusal direction and testing ablation, addition, and related causal interventions, and reports results across new models and a tool-use setting. The original refusal-direction method is cited as the basis.
record.gate_note: The README reports intervention outcomes, direction-signal comparisons, and behavioral outcomes. It also describes methods and lists output files; those file names alone are not treated as results. The AUC and text-versus-tool behavioral gap are recorded under fits_no_version because the claim versions do not specifically cover unsafe tool-call prediction or this transfer gap.
record.test_reason: The repo extracts a refusal direction and reports causal results in a new tool-use setting. Patching it into tool-mode runs partly restores refusal, and adding it induces over-refusal on benign prompts. The method is the cited one, but the setting (function-calling agents) is new, so this is T3 rather than T1. The source is a README only; ablation results from notebook 01 are described but not reported.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct, with two additions. The authors' headline is behavioural: in every model, text refusal did not carry over to tool calls, so text and tool safety need separate evaluations. Mechanistically, the direction predicts unsafe calls but is only a partial cause. Tools suppress the refusal signal in four of five models (not Llama-70B) and pull models toward acting. Steering cuts unsafe calls at a real over-refusal cost and is not a deployable defense.
record.recipe_differences: Research/evaluation repository, not described as a replication. It builds on the cited refusal-direction method but studies transfer to tool use and reports patching, steering, and tool-safety outcomes; the README does not state enough detail to confirm an exact match to the original extraction and intervention recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The tool-suppression result differs by model: it is reported in four of five models and is not significant for Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct. The README also says patching restoration varies by model (18 to 62 percent).

fits_no_version.finding: The refusal-direction projection is weaker when tools are present in four of five models; the drop is not significant for Llama-3.1-70B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Tool availability in the prompt suppresses activation of the refusal direction.

fits_no_version.finding: Projection onto the refusal direction predicts unsafe tool calls (AUC 0.69–0.88 across five models).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal-direction projection predicts unsafe agent tool calls.

fits_no_version.finding: Text refusal did not carry over to tool calls in any tested model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Chat-mode refusal does not transfer to tool-call actions.

fits_no_version.finding: Steering along the direction cuts unsafe tool calls, at an over-refusal cost.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal-direction steering reduces unsafe tool calls with a benign over-refusal tradeoff.

record.problems: The README gives several key outcomes only qualitatively or as ranges, without model-specific mappings or numerical baselines. It notes that the regex refusal classifier undercounts soft refusals, so exact rates are approximate. The repository text says bootstrap confidence intervals are used for follow-up analyses but does not provide the interval values for the summarized outcomes.
record.rows_left_out: No reported outcome rows were omitted. Listed notebook, script, and artifact files were not treated as results unless the README itself stated an outcome.

untested.parts: Ablation removing refusal: notebook 01 is said to check it, but the README gives no result. Retention of general abilities is not reported. Addition outside the benign over-refusal statement has no numbers.
No test of attacks suppressing the direction or of adversarial training against its ablation. The tool-enabled stress mode is not analysed for direction suppression in the README.
No test of multi-direction, cone or affine geometry.
No cross-language, cross-variant or base-to-instruct transfer of one direction.
Reasoning-mode behaviour is not examined, though Qwen3-14B can reason.

missing.what: Results of the causal check in notebook 01 (ablation removes refusal, addition induces it) per model
Per-model patching restoration rates and steering dose-response with bootstrap CIs
Ablation fix tests on small models (Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, gemma-3-4b-it)

record.verdict_notes: Only the README was read. The record's V4 link is removed: 'not one clean switch' refers to tool pull versus a suppressed signal, not to refusal geometry. The suppression finding is moved to fits_no_version. The authors warn that the regex refusal classifier undercounts soft refusals, so exact rates are approximate. The paper is unpublished and under review.

versions.untested_parts: The README does not report the difference-in-means extraction details, all-layer/all-position projection, no-tool ablation outcomes, or whether general abilities remain intact. It reports tool-mode patching and steering outcomes instead.
No weight-edit or abliteration result is reported.
No result tests attacks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
The README argues that the effect is not one clean switch, but does not test affine or cone geometry or identify additional refusal directions.
No separate harmfulness-judgment representation is tested.
The README does not test transfer of one direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct checkpoints.
No comparison of refusal-training procedures or timing is reported.
No reasoning models are identified or tested.
